multiplechoiceresponse.p: Five minutes into a live session the AI agent states something factually wrong. The best facilitation move is:

choice.div: Stop, and have the group check it against the source — turn it into a teaching moment.
Ignore it and carry on, so the session keeps to time.
Pretend it was part of the plan.

div.p: Correcting the model in the open models exactly the critical stance you are teaching: verify, do not trust.

multiplechoiceresponse.p: Before a live classroom session, you should always:

choice.div: Test the run end to end and have a non-AI fallback ready.
Assume it will work and prepare nothing else.
Let the learners discover the roles as they go.

div.p: Rehearse on the real material and keep a plan B. A gateway or classroom outage should not cost the session.

choiceresponse.p: Which keep the humans at the centre of a facilitated session? Select all that apply.

choice.div: Pausing the AI to discuss or question its output.
Assigning roles so a few voices do not dominate.
Letting the AI run the whole session unsupervised.
Offering a non-AI path for a learner who prefers it.

div.p: The AI is a foil for the learning, not the lesson. Facilitation is exactly the work of keeping the discussion with the people.
